subject: Copywriting
title: Cart Abandonment Emails
description: A micro-lesson that makes Cart Abandonment Emails usable.

hook.text: 70% of online shopping carts are abandoned. Cart emails recover 10-15% of them. That's billions in recovered revenue.

buildup.text: The first abandonment email should go out within one hour. After 24 hours, recovery rates drop by half.

discovery.text: The copy formula: remind what's in the cart, restate the benefit, add urgency.

twist.text: Three-email sequences recover 69% more revenue than single emails.

climax.text: Casper's cart email says: 'Come back to bed.' One line that captures the brand and the recovery in four words.

punchline.text: 'Come back to bed.' Four words recovering millions in revenue.

quiz.question: What percentage of online carts are abandoned?

details.summary: Cart abandonment emails recover revenue from shoppers who add items but leave without purchasing. They average a 45% open rate and recover 5-10% of abandoned carts. The best sequences use three emails: a reminder, a social proof nudge, and a final urgency message — often with a small discount.
details.whyItMatters: Nearly 70% of online shopping carts are abandoned. Automated recovery emails turn lost revenue into found money with minimal effort, making them the highest-ROI automated email.
takeaways: About 70% of online shopping carts are abandoned before purchase
Cart recovery emails average 45% open rates and 5-10% recovery rates
A three-email sequence outperforms a single reminder email

faq.question: What is the ideal timing for cart abandonment emails?
faq.answer: Send the first email within one hour of abandonment while intent is hot. Send a second email 24 hours later with social proof or reviews. Send a final email at 48-72 hours with urgency or a small discount. Waiting longer than 72 hours dramatically reduces recovery rates.

faq.question: Should cart abandonment emails always include a discount?
faq.answer: Not necessarily — starting with a discount trains customers to abandon carts on purpose. The first email should simply remind. The second should add social proof. Only the third might include a small discount if the item warrants it. Some brands recover carts without ever discounting.
